display.purpose: Major page headings and hero metrics.

shadows.name: panel-shadow
shadows.purpose: Lifts primary cards and panels slightly off the background.

shadows.name: interactive-shadow
shadows.purpose: Provides slight lift on interactive rows or actionable cards during hover states.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Tactile and confident primary action with moderate rounding.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background-color: #2f6b43; color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 16px; font-weight: 700; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s; font-family: Figtree, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #255737; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(47, 107, 67, .35); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Risk Badge (Critical)
components.description: Used to denote critical risk levels with crisp but slightly rounded edges.
components.css: .ds-badge-critical { background-color: #fbe8e6; color: #b53a32; padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 900; border-radius: 4px; display: inline-flex; font-family: Figtree, sans-serif; }

components.name: Card Panel
components.description: Structural container for primary focused metrics.
components.css: .ds-card-panel { background-color: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #dfe7df; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(34, 58, 39, 0.05); padding: 24px; font-family: Figtree, sans-serif; } .ds-card-eyebrow { color: #2f6b43; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; margin: 0 0 4px 0; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 900; color: #17241c; }

components.name: Secondary Context Area
components.description: Used for grouped information, filters, and supporting data.
components.css: .ds-context-panel { background-color: #F4F7F4; border: 1px solid #dfe7df; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; font-family: Figtree, sans-serif; } .ds-context-text { margin: 0; color: #66736a; font-size: 0.875rem; }

narrative.overview: AgriFlow AI serves as a precise, guided, and structured decision engine for agricultural operations. The visual language is earthy and confident, grounding the operator in the realities of the field while maintaining the clarity of a high-stakes logistics terminal. The interface prioritizes actionable signals—turning complex environmental and routing data into scannable queues and clear recommendations.
keyCharacteristics: Actionable density: Information is tightly packed but meticulously structured with strong visual rhythm.
Signal over noise: Color is reserved almost exclusively for status, risk, and primary actions.
Tabular precision: Numeric data uses tabular-nums for scannable comparison.
Restrained warmth: The interface feels precise but not rigid, warm but not soft, premium but not decorative.

rules.name: The Signal Isolation Rule
rules.body: Color is information, not decoration. The interface is largely monochromatic (ink, field white, sage) until a status or risk requires attention. Do not solve visual flatness by adding decorative colors, gradients, or glowing effects.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any numeric data meant to be compared vertically (metrics, scores, temperatures) must use tabular lining figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).

rules.name: The Surface Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Avoid making every content region a white card. Use Sage Surface (#F4F7F4) for secondary regions, contexts, or sidebars. Reserve elevated pure white panels for primary, focused content.

dos: Do use the established risk colors strictly for their semantic meaning (Green = Low, Amber = High, Red = Critical).
Do wrap primary interactive elements in the standard focus ring for accessibility.
Do use Sage Surface (#F4F7F4) to group secondary information and reduce the sea of white cards.
Do use moderate, restrained radii (6px–12px) to make the UI feel premium and approachable.
donts: Don't mandate 0px square corners for structural elements; the interface should not feel overly rigid or boxy.
Don't add excessive gradients, glassmorphism, glow effects, or generic AI SaaS aesthetics.
Don't make every piece of content a white card. Use surface hierarchy to differentiate primary and secondary data.
